item.text:
**5B.1 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning negative. Srettha did back some long-run, productive-growth policies and investment promotion, but his defining domestic economic move was the very large digital-wallet cash transfer, which was widely framed as short-term stimulus and attracted fiscal-risk criticism. I found no direct 2024 evidence that he personally used economic policy to extract rents, but the evidence is stronger for popularity-seeking stimulus than for a clearly sustainable prosperity strategy.

- [Thailand Systematic Country Diagnostic Update 2024: Shifting Gears - Toward Sustainable Growth and Inclusive Prosperity](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/thailand/publication/thailand-scd2024) | World Bank | March 1, 2024 | The World Bank laid out a long-horizon reform agenda centered on human capital, innovation, secondary cities, climate-resilient development, and stronger fiscal institutions and public finance. This is strong positive evidence for a broad-based, sustainable prosperity frame. | QIDs: 5B.1

- [Mr. Narit Therdsteerasukdi, Secretary General of the Thailand Board of Investment (BOI) accompanied Mr. Srettha Thavisin, Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, on a visit to Australia](https://www.boi.go.th/en/boi_event_detail/?module=activity&topic_id=135122) | Thailand Board of Investment | March 4-6, 2024 | Srettha went on an investment-promotion trip to Australia to discuss Thailand’s investment policies, business facilitation, and opportunities with major firms. This supports an intent to attract productive investment rather than simply distribute patronage. | QIDs: 5B.1

- [Thailand's Jan-March Investment Pledges Soar 31% to USD6.2 Billion, Signaling Strong Year Ahead, BOI Says](https://www.boi.go.th/un/boi_event_detail?language=en&module=news&topic_id=135253) | Thailand Board of Investment | 2024 | BOI reported a 31 percent jump in first-quarter investment applications, led by electronics, automotive, digital, and other productive sectors. That is positive evidence for a growth strategy aimed at tradable, higher-value activity. | QIDs: 5B.1

- [Thailand Economic Monitor July 2024: Unlocking the Growth Potential of Secondary Cities](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/thailand/publication/temjuly2024) | World Bank | July 3, 2024 | The World Bank projected 2.4 percent growth but warned that public debt and the fiscal deficit would rise as stimulus measures were implemented, and it urged more targeted social assistance and higher tax revenue. This is mixed evidence: it shows concern for sustainability, but also that the policy mix relied on costly stimulus. | QIDs: 5B.1

- [Thailand's cabinet approves $13.5 billion digital-wallet handout](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007) | Reuters via Investing.com | April 23, 2024 | Reuters described the 500 billion baht digital-wallet plan as a 10,000-baht cash transfer for 50 million Thais. That is strong negative evidence for short-term popularity-seeking: it was broad, highly visible, and fiscally controversial rather than narrowly targeted to long-run productivity. | QIDs: 5B.1

- [Thailand's flagship $14 billion handout faces delays and criticism](https://www.yahoo.com/news/thailands-flagship-14-billion-handout-072635149.html) | Reuters via Yahoo News | August 1, 2024 | Reuters reported implementation snags and criticism from economists and former central bankers who called the scheme fiscally risky. This strengthens the negative side by showing the flagship program was not just popular, but also vulnerable on sustainability grounds. | QIDs: 5B.1

- **Search gap** | N/A | N/A | I found no direct 2024 source showing Srettha personally extracting rents, redirecting state money to insiders, or explicitly framing policy around loyalty-buying. The strongest negative evidence is indirect: the universal cash-transfer scheme, its political salience, and the repeated fiscal-risk criticism. | QIDs: 5B.1
